+# EXF-000 — Subject truth: what Expanding Frontiers actually is and what it can award
+
+**Node:** `EXF-000` · **Round:** R1 · **Role:** Explorer
+**Stopping condition:** the award surface, its funders, and the eligibility path are documented with sources, and unverifiable claims are labeled.
+
+## 0. Evidence boundary (read this before trusting anything below)
+
+`expandingfrontiers.org` could not be fetched from this session: the organization's
+network egress proxy blocked the domain (`EGRESS_BLOCKED`). Every fact below therefore
+comes from **secondary sources** — search-indexed page summaries, NASA, NSS, DOE/EDA,
+and Rio Grande Valley press. Nothing here was read off the organization's own live site.
+
+That matters for a specific reason: **deadlines, prize amounts, cohort dates, and
+eligibility rules are exactly the class of fact that goes stale first**, and they are
+the facts a submission depends on. They are marked `UNVERIFIED` throughout and are
+carried forward as operator confirmations in `09_SUBMISSION_PLAN.md`.
+
+## 1. The organization
+
+| Property | Value | Confidence |
+|---|---|---|
+| Legal form | 501(c)(3) non-profit | Verified |
+| Founded | 2019, Brownsville, Texas | Verified |
+| Founder | Fredrick Jenet, PhD (astrophysicist) | Verified |
+| Thesis | Build an innovation ecosystem for **space and energy** technology in South Texas | Verified |
+| Geography | Brownsville / Rio Grande Valley — ~20 miles west of SpaceX Starbase | Verified |
+| Posture | Signed the Washington Compact on Norms of Behavior for Commercial Space Operations (Sept 2025) | Verified |
+
+The single most important structural fact: **ExF is a non-profit intermediary, not a
+fund.** It does not primarily award its own money. It wins grants *from* federal and
+philanthropic funders and converts them into programs, and it routes companies toward
+licensable technology and follow-on capital. Anyone optimizing an entry for ExF is
+really optimizing for **what makes ExF's own funders renew ExF**.
+
+## 2. The programs (the entry surface)
+
+| Program | What it is | Confidence |
+|---|---|---|
+| **ExF Accelerator** | Helps founders turn space, energy and adjacent ideas into companies | Verified |
+| **NASA Tech Trek** | Six-month program run under a **Space Act Agreement with NASA Johnson Space Center**; ExF acts as a "concierge of NASA technologies" for Brownsville, moving NASA IP to regional entrepreneurs | Verified |
+| **Rockets & Rigs** | Statewide cross-industry initiative uniting the **commercial space** and **oil & gas / energy** industries to find shared problems and commercialize shared solutions | Verified |
+| **Entrepreneur in Residence Apprenticeship (EIRA)** | Apprenticeship for aspiring entrepreneurs/"astropreneurs" in South Texas | Verified |
+| **Veterans Ascension** | Places highly trained veterans into commercial space careers | Verified |
+| **Space Entrepreneur Summer Academy (SESA)** | Three-week immersive high-school program | Verified |
+| Current 2026 cohort dates / open calls | — | **UNVERIFIED** |
+
+## 3. The award mechanism
+
+The **ExF Space Tech Pitch Competition** is the competitive event this subject targets.
+
+- Entrants pitch to a panel of industry leaders, investors and experts.
+- Outcomes include visibility, feedback, mentorship, and **non-dilutive seed funding / cash prizes**.
+- Historically the field is drawn from **EIRA and NASA Tech Trek graduates**, pitching
+  commercial products developed from **licensed NASA technologies**.
+- First annual edition: 9 December 2021, at ExF's Brownsville facilities. A dedicated
+  2024 competition site existed (`exfspacetechppitchcomp2024.org`).
+- 2026 prize pool, dates, and eligibility: **UNVERIFIED**.
+
+**Consequence for candidate selection.** The pipeline is not "have a good startup idea."
+The pipeline is: *enter a program → get matched to a NASA technology → build a commercial
+product on it → pitch it.* An idea with no plausible NASA technology-transfer anchor is
+entering against the grain of the mechanism that actually selects.
+
+## 4. Who pays ExF (the real judging function)
+
+| Funder / award | Detail | Confidence |
+|---|---|---|
+| **U.S. Department of Energy — EPIC Prize** | $50,000, one of 20 incubators/accelerators nationally; explicitly supported **Rockets & Rigs** | Verified |
+| **National Space Society**, funded by **Blue Origin's Club for the Future** | STEM education grant (2022) for the Brownsville Summer Entrepreneur Academy | Verified |
+| **U.S. Economic Development Administration** | STEM Talent Challenge (2020) | Verified |
+| **U.S. Small Business Administration** | 2025 Growth Accelerator Fund Competition awardee — **Capital Formation** category, for expanding investment access in South Texas | Verified |
+| **NASA JSC** | Space Act Agreement (technology transfer, not cash) | Verified |
+| **Brownsville Community Improvement Corporation (BCIC)** | Local economic-development backing | Verified |
+
+Read the column of funders and the selection function falls out of it. DOE bought the
+**space × energy intersection**. SBA bought **capital formation in South Texas**. EDA
+bought **regional STEM talent**. NASA supplied **licensable technology**. Blue Origin/NSS
+bought **local workforce pipeline**. Every one of those is a *regional economic outcome*
+or a *technology-transfer outcome* — not a generic "is this a good startup" judgment.
+
+## 5. Local physical context (August 2026)
+
+This is the operating environment any winning entry is implicitly promising to serve:
+
+- **Starbase**, ~20 miles east of Brownsville, sits on a narrow ridge of high ground
+  strung through **tidal wetlands** on the Rio Grande floodplain — a salt-spray,
+  high-humidity, high-corrosion coastal environment.
+- SpaceX is building **"Starpipe"**, an eight-mile natural gas pipeline from the **Port of
+  Brownsville** to Starbase, paired with an **on-site liquefaction facility** under Army
+  Corps of Engineers review.
+- Starship's Raptor engines burn liquid methane; **each launch consumes roughly 630,000
+  gallons**, currently delivered by tanker truck.
+- FAA and the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) have monitored the site's
+  safety and environmental impact since 2014; launch-pad particulate emissions have drawn
+  published academic measurement work.
+- On 25 August 2026 SpaceX announced a **$100B Starship spaceport in Louisiana**, which
+  both validates the sector and raises the question of whether South Texas keeps its
+  centre-of-gravity — a live anxiety for exactly the regional funders listed above.
+
+That last point is a selection signal, not colour. A 2026 entry that **deepens the reason
+industry stays anchored in the Rio Grande Valley** is arguing directly to what ExF's
+funders are worried about this year.
+
+## 6. What could not be verified
+
+1. The live contents of `expandingfrontiers.org` (egress-blocked).
+2. Whether any program or pitch competition is **currently open** for 2026.
+3. Prize amounts, deadlines, residency and eligibility requirements.
+4. Whether a specific NASA technology is presently available for license.
+5. Whether ExF requires prior EIRA/Tech Trek participation to enter the pitch competition,
+   or accepts external entrants.
+
+All five are carried into `09_SUBMISSION_PLAN.md` as blocking operator confirmations.
+

+# EXF-010 — Scouted candidate field
+
+**Node:** `EXF-010` · **Round:** R2 (parallel with EXF-020) · **Roles:** Explorer, Architect
+**Stopping condition:** additional scouting produces duplicates or dominated variants rather than materially new mechanisms, and that saturation is recorded.
+
+Scouting was scoped by the subject truth: candidates must be enterable into an Expanding
+Frontiers program by a South Texas applicant, and must plausibly reach a cash prize or
+grant. Twenty-seven candidates across five mechanism families survived a first pass;
+filler was not manufactured to reach a count.
+
+## Family A — Evidence, software and data
+
+| # | Candidate | Mechanism | Buyer | Why it belongs |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| A1 | Tamper-evident assurance receipts for AI-authored safety-critical code | Sealed, independently re-executed checks producing a signed receipt bundle | Launch and energy operators, their auditors and insurers | The applicant already owns a working implementation |
+| A2 | Launch-site environmental compliance evidence platform | Continuous particulate / acoustic / wildlife capture bound to a tamper-evident record | Operators filing to FAA and TCEQ | Published academic work shows a real measurement gap at this site |
+| A3 | Cryogenic ground-support-equipment predictive maintenance | ML on cryo pump/valve telemetry | Launch operators, LNG terminals | Shared failure surface between rockets and rigs |
+| A4 | Methane liquefaction plant anomaly detection | Process telemetry anomaly models | Starbase liquefaction, Port terminals | Directly on the new Starpipe infrastructure |
+| A5 | Digital-thread parts provenance for launch supply chain | Cryptographic part pedigree | Tier-2 suppliers | Counterfeit/traceability is a real aerospace cost |
+| A6 | Range and road-closure logistics optimiser | Scheduling under closure constraints | Cameron County, local haulers | Locally acute, commercially thin |
+| A7 | Space-weather to grid-operator alerting | GIC forecasting for ERCOT | Grid operators | Space × energy, but a crowded incumbent field |
+| A8 | Sensor-derived launch damage claim adjudication | Evidence pipeline for insurers | Space insurers | Narrow buyer, long sales cycle |
+
+## Family B — NASA-licensable hardware and materials
+
+| # | Candidate | NASA anchor | Buyer | Why it belongs |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| B1 | **Smart corrosion-detecting and self-inhibiting coating** | KSC "Coatings and Methods for Corrosion Detection and/or Reduction" (KSC-TOPS-1) — microcapsule-released inhibitors and indicators | Coastal launch structures, Port of Brownsville steel, pipelines, LNG tankage | Exact NASA-license archetype the pitch competition selects for; the local environment is a salt-marsh corrosion worst case |
+| B2 | Hydrogen-sensing tape for cryogenic lines | KSC-invented hydrogen-sensing tape (previously licensed to UCF) | Hydrogen energy, cryo transfer | Real NASA IP; hydrogen demand in Texas is growing |
+| B3 | Leak-proof composite cryogenic valve | NASA low-mass cryogenic valve, already field-installed at a methane coal-gas field | Methane fields, propellant transfer | Precedent of exactly this space-to-gas-field transfer |
+| B4 | Aerogel / advanced insulation for LCH4 and LNG storage | NASA cryogenic insulation portfolio | Liquefaction and storage | Boil-off is a direct cash loss |
+| B5 | Electrostatic dust and particulate mitigation | NASA electrodynamic dust shield lineage | Oilfield and launch-pad equipment | Transfers cleanly, modest market |
+| B6 | Soil/regolith stabilisation for coastal erosion | NASA regolith stabilisation work | Coastal infrastructure | Weak commercial pull |
+| B7 | Water reclamation for colonias | NASA ECLSS water recovery | Rural Rio Grande Valley water systems | Very high social value, weak buyer |
+| B8 | Additive manufacture of cryogenic components | NASA AM process IP | GSE suppliers | Capital heavy |
+
+## Family C — Energy × space process plays
+
+| # | Candidate | Mechanism | Why it belongs |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| C1 | **Boil-off recovery and reliquefaction** for LCH4 at Starbase and LNG at the Port | Capture and reliquefy vapour that is currently lost or flared | Purest Rockets & Rigs thesis; ~630,000 gal of LCH4 per Starship launch makes losses material |
+| C2 | Flare-gas to propellant-grade methane purification | Take stranded/flared Permian gas to rocket-grade spec | Turns an energy waste stream into a space input |
+| C3 | Modular bio/e-methane for propellant | Renewable propellant feedstock | Strong narrative, brutal economics |
+| C4 | Launch-operations microgrid and storage | Islanded power for launch campaigns | Real need, commodity solution |
+| C5 | Waste-heat recovery on liquefaction trains | Efficiency retrofit | Incremental |
+| C6 | Hydrogen from stranded gas | Pyrolysis / reforming | Capital intensive |
+
+## Family D — Workforce and services
+
+| # | Candidate | Why it belongs |
+|---|---|---|
+| D1 | Veterans-to-space-industry credentialing platform | Maps directly onto Veterans Ascension and EDA talent money |
+| D2 | Bilingual space-technician training pipeline | Direct regional workforce impact |
+| D3 | Launch tourism and visitor experience | Real local revenue, no technology transfer |
+
+## Family E — Bio and environment
+
+| # | Candidate | Why it belongs |
+|---|---|---|
+| E1 | Microgravity agriculture payload service | Space-adjacent, no energy leg |
+| E2 | Coastal fisheries and wetland monitoring | Regionally resonant, buyer unclear |
+
+## Saturation record
+
+Scouting was continued until new searching returned materially the same mechanisms.
+Saturation was declared on three signals:
+
+1. **Mechanism repetition.** New candidates collapsed into families already represented —
+   further "space × energy" ideas reduced to variants of C1/C2, further NASA-transfer
+   ideas to variants of B1–B4.
+2. **Dominance.** Late candidates were dominated on the rubric by an existing entrant in
+   the same family (e.g. C5 waste-heat recovery is dominated by C1 on every criterion).
+3. **Off-thesis drift.** Broader searching produced generic space startups with no South
+   Texas anchor, which the regional-impact veto eliminates before scoring.
+
+Twenty-seven candidates is a deliberate stopping point, not a target: the families are
+exhaustive of the mechanisms ExF's programs can actually route a company through
+(license NASA IP, join space to energy, build regional workforce, sell software/data).

+# EXF-020 — The evaluation system, derived from sponsor behaviour
+
+**Node:** `EXF-020` · **Round:** R2 (parallel with EXF-010) · **Roles:** Architect, Curator
+**Stopping condition:** criteria, weights, and the veto rule are fixed and justified against sponsor evidence before any candidate is scored.
+
+## Why not a generic startup rubric
+
+A generic rubric (market size / team / traction / moat) would rank these candidates the
+way a seed VC would. That is the wrong judging function. The money at the end of this
+funnel is **non-dilutive**: DOE prize money, SBA capital-formation money, EDA talent
+money, NASA technology-transfer access, and a non-profit's cash prizes. Non-dilutive
+funders do not buy equity upside. They buy **their own mission outcomes**.
+
+Every criterion below traces to an observed funding behaviour from `01_SUBJECT_TRUTH.md`,
+not to intuition.
+
+## Criteria and weights
+
+| # | Criterion | Weight | Traced to |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| 1 | **NASA technology-transfer fit** — can this be built on an actual licensable NASA technology? | **0.18** | Space Act Agreement with NASA JSC; NASA Tech Trek; pitch-competition entrants historically pitch *licensed NASA technologies* |
+| 2 | **Space × energy intersection** — does it serve both industries, not one? | **0.16** | DOE EPIC Prize was awarded *specifically* to fund Rockets & Rigs |
+| 3 | **Regional economic impact** — jobs, capital and activity that land in South Texas | **0.15** | EDA STEM Talent Challenge; SBA GAFC Capital Formation; BCIC backing |
+| 4 | **Non-dilutive follow-on path** — a named next cheque (SBIR/STTR/DOE/NASA/state) | **0.13** | SBA GAFC *Capital Formation* category; an accelerator is judged on where its companies go next |
+| 5 | **Demonstrability at a pitch** — can a judge *see* it work in ten minutes? | **0.12** | The award mechanism is a live pitch competition before non-technical investors and industry leaders |
+| 6 | **Founder asset advantage** — what already exists in the applicant's hands | **0.10** | Prizes reward credible execution, not proposals; ExF's own value proposition is speed to a real company |
+| 7 | **Capital efficiency to first revenue** | **0.08** | Prize sizes are modest (ExF's own flagship win was $50k); an idea that needs $5M before it does anything cannot be started with the award |
+| 8 | **Regulatory and safety headroom** — how much permitting stands between award and revenue | **0.08** | FAA/TCEQ/Army Corps scrutiny is continuous at this site; a prize cannot shorten a multi-year permit |
+
+Weights sum to **1.00**.
+
+## The veto rule
+
+Weighted averages hide fatal flaws. Two criteria are therefore **vetoes**, not weights:
+
+> An entrant scoring **≤ 3 / 10** on **regional economic impact (#3)** or on
+> **regulatory and safety headroom (#8)** is eliminated regardless of its weighted score.
+
+- **#3 is a veto** because a non-profit funded by EDA, SBA and a municipal improvement
+  corporation cannot champion something with no South Texas footprint. It is not a
+  scoring penalty for them; it is disqualifying.
+- **#8 is a veto** because prize money cannot buy a permit. An idea whose first revenue
+  sits behind an Army Corps or FAA approval converts an award into a waiting room.
+
+## Scoring scale
+
+0–10 per criterion. Weighted score = Σ(score × weight). Scores are evidence-anchored
+where evidence exists and are labelled as judgement where it does not; where evidence is
+weak the confidence is lowered rather than the number invented.
+
+## What this rubric deliberately does *not* reward
+
+- **Market size in the abstract.** A trillion-dollar TAM slide does not move a
+  regional-impact funder.
+- **Novelty for its own sake.** NASA technology transfer rewards *transfer*, not invention.
+- **Pure software elegance.** Software with no physical or regional footprint scores 0.18
+  and 0.16 near zero and will usually trip the #3 veto.
+
+That third point is the rubric's sharpest edge, and it is aimed at the most tempting
+candidates in the field.

+## Veto outcomes
+
+| Entrant | Vetoing criterion | Why it is a veto and not a penalty |
+|---|---|---|
+| **T4** Flare-gas to propellant | `regulatory_headroom` = 3 | Gas processing and propellant-spec production sit behind TCEQ air permitting and pipeline authority. No prize shortens that. The award would fund a waiting room. |

+applicant's own asset.** The strongest thing in the applicant's hands — a working

+and 9 on founder advantage, capital efficiency and regulatory headroom, and still fails,

+technology* and *what happens in South Texas*.
+
+That does not mean the asset is worthless here. It means the asset is a **component**,
+not an entry. Round two tests whether pairing it with a physical, licensable, locally
+anchored technology survives attack — which is exactly what T1 and T3 are.

+T3 on mechanism and by T2 on domain; T9 scores 10 on regional impact but 1 on NASA

+# EXF-050 — Round two: adversarial battles
+
+**Node:** `EXF-050` · **Round:** R5 · **Roles:** Architect, Curator
+**Stopping condition:** every leading entrant has faced a scenario built to defeat it and the outcome is recorded with a fundamental-or-fixable verdict.
+
+Each surviving entrant is attacked with the scenario most likely to kill it. Triple
+elimination is the point: an entrant is not removed for one narrow weakness, only for a
+weakness that is **fundamental** — one that cannot be engineered around within the
+programme's reach.
+
+---
+
+## T1 · Corrosion-evidence coating
+
+**Attack A — "The patent is not yours to have."**
+NASA's KSC corrosion coating may be exclusively licensed, dormant, or unavailable in
+2026. Without the license the entrant collapses to a software wrapper.
+→ **Fundamental if true, but it is a fact, not a flaw.** It is checkable in one enquiry
+through the NASA T2 portal and, more directly, through ExF's own Space Act Agreement —
+which is precisely the service ExF exists to provide. Carried as blocking confirmation
+`C-1`. If it fails, an equivalent NASA corrosion-sensing or coatings technology
+substitutes; if none exists, T1 degrades to T3.
+
+**Attack B — "Industrial coatings is a commodity market owned by giants."**
+PPG, AkzoNobel, Sherwin-Williams and Hempel own coastal and marine protective coatings.
+A South Texas startup does not win on coating chemistry.
+→ **Fixable, and the attack actually sharpens the entry.** The entrant should not sell
+coating chemistry. The coating is the *sensor*; the product is the **inspection record**:
+a defensible, tamper-evident corrosion history per asset, per inspection, per date. The
+incumbents sell a can. This sells an auditable answer to "prove the asset was sound on
+this date" — which is what insurers, regulators and asset buyers actually pay for.
+Repositioned, the giants become channel partners rather than competitors.
+
+**Attack C — "Coating qualification takes years."**
+Getting into an owner's approved-products specification is a multi-year process.
+→ **Real wound, partially fixable.** Mitigation: enter through inspection pilots on
+secondary structures and existing coated assets, where the indicator is applied as a
+monitoring layer rather than replacing the protective system. Revenue starts as
+inspection services, not as coating sales. This is the entrant's largest genuine risk
+and it is recorded as such rather than argued away.
+
+**Verdict: advances, wounded on Attack C, blocked on confirmation C-1.**
+
+---
+
+## T3 · Compliance evidence platform
+
+**Attack A — "You are selling surveillance to the surveilled."**
+The obvious buyer is the operator whose emissions and noise you are measuring. Operators
+do not buy independent, tamper-evident evidence of their own performance. Regulators

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""EXF-040 scorer: recomputes every weighted score from published inputs.
+
+Run from the repository root:
+    python docs/plan/expanding-frontiers-2026-08-28/score.py
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+WEIGHTS = {
+    "nasa_tech_transfer_fit": 0.18,
+    "space_energy_intersection": 0.16,
+    "regional_economic_impact": 0.15,
+    "non_dilutive_follow_on": 0.13,
+    "demonstrability_at_pitch": 0.12,
+    "founder_asset_advantage": 0.10,
+    "capital_efficiency": 0.08,
+    "regulatory_headroom": 0.08,
+}
+VETO_CRITERIA = ("regional_economic_impact", "regulatory_headroom")
+VETO_THRESHOLD = 3
+
+ENTRANTS = {
+    "T1": ("Corrosion-evidence coating", [10, 9, 9, 8, 10, 7, 6, 7]),
+    "T2": ("Cryogenic boil-off recovery", [8, 10, 9, 8, 4, 2, 2, 4]),
+    "T3": ("Compliance evidence platform", [4, 8, 6, 7, 8, 9, 9, 8]),
+    "T4": ("Flare-gas to propellant", [5, 10, 7, 7, 3, 1, 2, 3]),
+    "T5": ("Hydrogen-sensing tape", [9, 8, 5, 6, 8, 1, 6, 6]),
+    "T6": ("Cryo GSE predictive maintenance", [4, 9, 5, 6, 6, 5, 8, 8]),
+    "T7": ("Composite cryogenic valve", [9, 10, 5, 7, 6, 1, 4, 5]),
+    "T8": ("AI-code assurance receipts (standalone)", [2, 3, 2, 6, 7, 10, 10, 9]),
+    "T9": ("Veterans credentialing platform", [1, 6, 10, 8, 5, 2, 8, 9]),
+    "T10": ("Space-weather grid alerting", [7, 9, 4, 6, 7, 3, 8, 8]),
+}
+
+
+def evaluate() -> list[dict]:
+    assert abs(sum(WEIGHTS.values()) - 1.0) < 1e-9, "weights must sum to 1.0"
+    names = list(WEIGHTS)
+    rows = []
+    for key, (title, values) in ENTRANTS.items():
+        assert len(values) == len(names), f"{key} score vector length mismatch"
+        scores = dict(zip(names, values))
+        weighted = round(sum(scores[n] * WEIGHTS[n] for n in names), 4)
+        vetoes = [c for c in VETO_CRITERIA if scores[c] <= VETO_THRESHOLD]
+        rows.append(
+            {
+                "id": key,
+                "name": title,
+                "scores": scores,
+                "weighted_score": weighted,
+                "vetoed": bool(vetoes),
+                "veto_criteria": vetoes,
+            }
+        )
+    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["vetoed"], -r["weighted_score"]))
+    for rank, row in enumerate(rows, start=1):
+        row["round1_rank"] = rank if not row["vetoed"] else None
+    return rows
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    results = evaluate()
+    width = max(len(r["name"]) for r in results)
+    print(f"{'ID':<4} {'ENTRANT':<{width}}  {'WEIGHTED':>8}  {'RANK':>4}  STATUS")
+    for row in results:
+        status = "VETOED: " + ", ".join(row["veto_criteria"]) if row["vetoed"] else "advanced"
+        rank = row["round1_rank"] or "-"
+        print(f"{row['id']:<4} {row['name']:<{width}}  {row['weighted_score']:>8.4f}  {rank:>4}  {status}")
+    Path(__file__).with_name("round1_scores.json").write_text(
+        json.dumps({"weights": WEIGHTS, "veto_threshold": VETO_THRESHOLD,
+                    "veto_criteria": list(VETO_CRITERIA), "results": results},
+                   indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n",
+        encoding="utf-8",
+    )
